about: Research pass for part 2 and part 3 of the talk (the editor's 17:37 request). (a) The open source strategy lives on its own site, open-source.sgit.ai ('Open source is a strategy. It is not a charity.'), with the position, founder guidance, funding and survivability pages; the business model shows on sgit.ai/investors (the code is free, the running service is sold) and in newsroom.sgit.ai articles on what open source is, who pays, the maintenance deficit and the fork. (b) No page is titled 'investment workflows'; the closest match is the newsroom brief investor.sgit.ai (deal rooms as vaults, contracts as graphs, funding models, an evaluation framework for GenAI security startups), with where-to-invest-in-sgit, sell-don't-issue and the-fork-next-door as the investment models; investor.sgit.ai itself is not built. (c) On the PHP October site: one reported (unconfirmed) case of firewalls rooted through php2shell, ten security products marked vulnerable, two security vendors' compromise claims withdrawn, and in its Pulse section six security products on the KEV list this month (BeyondTrust, SiteGuard WAF, PAN-OS, Fortinet, Ivanti VPN, Cisco email gateway). Gaps: sharness.ai, pki.sgit.ai and the blog were not searched further (covered by other catalogues); open-source.sgit.ai pages have no infographics; charts on open-source-is-not-free were lazy-loaded and not captured.
cautions: No page on newsroom.sgit.ai is called 'investment workflows'; investor-sgit-ai.html is offered as the match. Confirm with the editor before a slide calls it that.
investor.sgit.ai did not resolve at capture (proxy 502); the brief says none of it is built yet. Do not show it as a live site.
The Dream Research case is one vendor's unconfirmed account; the newsroom says no victim, firewall vendor, agency or CISA has confirmed it. Say 'reported', never 'happened'.
The 'ten security products' are vulnerable, not exploited. Keep the two apart on a slide.

The Pulse cases (BeyondTrust, SiteGuard, PAN-OS, Fortinet, Ivanti, Cisco) are not PHP: Pulse is a separate section about this month's KEV additions. They answer 'security products are being attacked', not 'PHP hit security products'.
The CVE numbers on the PHP site are as the site gives them; not checked against NVD.
The Dream Research article narrates the attack in some detail (targeting, chain); use only the headline and the framing, no technique.
Pulse pages show vendor PSIRT email addresses in their measurement lines; none is quoted or cropped here.
The open-source.sgit.ai crop shows the byline with a 'LinkedIn' link label; no URL or contact detail is visible. Crop it out if the editor prefers.
PHP site pages have moved to subdomains (updates. and refs.php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai); old URLs redirect. Use the final_url.
The maintenance-deficit crop is Dion Wiggins' illustration; check reuse before it goes on a slide.
The Dream Research article page shows a live data notice (site data moved on since it was written).

pieces.title: Open source is a strategy. It is not a charity.
pieces.what_it_says: The editor's open source strategy site: open source is not generosity but strategy; technology stops being the moat, you are free to delete your own code, sovereignty becomes possible, and what is sold is trust.

pieces.title: The position: open source is a strategy, not a charity
pieces.what_it_says: The full position with counter-cases: technology is not the moat; lock-in relocates to quality, certification and maintainability; open source frees you to cannibalise your own code; "We are selling trust."

pieces.title: Owning the code, or opening it: guidance for founders
pieces.what_it_says: Field notes for a solo founder: what copying your code would really cost an incumbent, four instincts and their counter-arguments, explorers, villagers and town planners, and eight steps in order.

pieces.title: Funding: three proposals, compared for the first time, and a position
pieces.what_it_says: Three ways to fund open source (market forces and supply-chain labelling, a maintainer platform, sovereignty bounties) side by side, with a position on how they fit.

pieces.title: Survivability is not a property of the licence file
pieces.what_it_says: Every relicensing from 2018 to 2024 followed one pattern: a single corporate copyright holder used a CLA to change terms; distributed copyright could not be moved that way.

pieces.title: Somebody has to be the villagers: maintenance as a market
pieces.what_it_says: Maintaining the non-functional requirements (security, backups, reliability) of software others wrote is a market, and reading and repairing code is an appreciating scarce asset.
